blocks.value: Lesson 12 said a class is a blueprint. This lesson is where you actually draw one.

The central idea is **encapsulation**: an object keeps its data private and exposes only the operations it chooses to allow. That sounds bureaucratic until you see what it prevents, a `BankAccount` whose balance can be set to −5,000 from anywhere in the program.
What you will be able to do
By the end of this lesson you will be able to:

items: Write a class with instance variables and methods
Distinguish instance variables from local variables
Apply `public` and `private` to hide implementation details
